A powerful nor'easter has struck the U.S. Northeast, bringing torrential rain, destructive winds, and coastal flooding that inundated roads and homes.

Social Physics Analysis:
Natural hazards present unavoidable physical stress tests where actors either cooperate transparently through emergency response or retreat into isolated panic. Public agencies and utilities align toward restoration and physical safety.

Actual Article Body:
PROVIDENCE, Rhode Island (AP) — More than 70,000 customers were without electricity in the U.S. Northeast on Saturday, the effect of a powerful nor’easter expected to create dangerous conditions through the weekend. Forecasters warned of gale winds that could down trees and heavy rain that could put roads underwater.

Tens of millions of people are in the path of the storm, which was already beginning to lash the region. Dangerous flooding is expected along the Mid-Atlantic coast, particularly near New Jersey and Delaware, according to the National Weather Service.

Stated Claim / Post Context:
New Jersey company recalls nearly 333 pounds of tuna over high histamine levels

Buckhead Meat Company, doing business as Trinity Seafood in Lakewood, voluntarily launched the recall on July 24.

Actual Article Body:
Switch between CA and NY editions here.

See more of our coverage in your search results.

A New Jersey seafood company has recalled nearly 333 pounds of tuna distributed across five states after health officials found high levels of a toxin linked to histamine poisoning.

Buckhead Meat Company, doing business as Trinity Seafood in Lakewood, voluntarily launched the recall on July 24 after the New Jersey Department of Health notified the company that two tuna samples had tested for high levels of scombrotoxin.

Scombrotoxin can cause scombroid poisoning, with symptoms appearing within minutes to two hours and often resembling an allergic reaction, including facial flushing, sweating, dizziness, nausea, headache, hives and abdominal cramps.

Severe cases can cause blurred vision, respiratory distress and swelling of the tongue, according to the FDA.

The FDA formally classified the action as a Class II recall on Sept. 16 — nearly eight weeks
